'''Business and economy'''
*[[Unemployment in the United States]]
**Several global [[financial market]]s fall significantly, with the [[Dow Jones Industrial Average|Dow Jones]] falling by 610 points after the [[United States Department of Labor]] reported that the [[Unemployment in the United States|unemployment]] rate increased to 4.3% in July, the highest since October 2021. [https://apnews.com/article/economy-jobs-unemployment-federal-reserve-inflation-22095766804d9c1532b4fcc29565be49 (AP)]

*At least 11 people are killed in a fire in a [[Residential building|residential]]-[[commercial building]] in [[Manila]], [[Philippines]]. [https://www.thestar.com.my/aseanplus/aseanplus-news/2024/08/02/building-fire-in-manila039s-chinatown-kills-11 (''The Star'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[2024 Venezuelan presidential election]], [[Argentina–Venezuela relations]]
**[[Argentina]] recognizes [[Edmundo González Urrutia|Edmundo González]] as [[President of Venezuela|President-elect of Venezuela]], becoming the third country to do so after the [[United States]] and [[Peru]]. [https://www.barrons.com/news/argentina-recognizes-venezuela-opposition-candidate-as-president-elect-minister-7bcf778d (AFP via ''Barron's'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2024 United Kingdom riots]]
**[[Riot]]ing occurs in [[Sunderland]], [[England]], [[United Kingdom]], as hundreds of [[Far-right politics in the United Kingdom|far-right]] protesters attempt to march on a [[mosque]] and clash with [[Northumbria Police|riot police]] in the city centre. A [[police station]] and [[Citizens Advice]] bureau is [[arson|set on fire]] by rioters. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cnl0lkrxgvxo (BBC News)]
*[[Censorship in Turkey]]
**[[Turkey]] blocks [[internet access]] to [[Instagram]], following comments made by Turkish [[Directorate of Communications|communications director]] [[Fahrettin Altun]] that condemned [[Meta Platforms]] for taking down Instagram posts offering condolences or expressing sorrow towards the [[Assassination of Ismail Haniyeh|assassination]] of [[Hamas]] political leader [[Ismail Haniyeh]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/turkey-blocks-access-instagram-platform-gives-no-reason-2024-08-02/ (Reuters)]
*[[Mass surveillance in the United Kingdom]]
**Several [[Civil and political rights|civil rights groups]] denounce proposals made by [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|British Prime Minister]] [[Keir Starmer]] to grant [[Law enforcement in the United Kingdom|British police]] nationalized [[Facial recognition system|live facial recognition technology]] and [[surveillance]] to [[criminal charge|charge]] people police consider significantly likely to participate in [[Far-right politics in the United Kingdom|far-right]] riots, condemning the [[opportunism]] of the proposals, their potential racial and gender inaccuracy, and their possible use to target future legal protests. [https://www.theguardian.com/technology/article/2024/aug/02/starmer-live-facial-recognition-plan-would-usher-in-national-id-campaigners-warn (''The Guardian'')]
*A man is arrested by [[Garda Síochána|national police]] in [[Dublin]], [[Ireland]], following attacks on [[Government Buildings]], [[The Custom House]], and [[Áras an Uachtaráin]]. [https://www.rte.ie/news/ireland/2024/0802/1463156-government-buildings/ (RTÉ)]
*Four men, including a police officer, are found shot to death near [[Cancún]], [[Quintana Roo]], [[Mexico]]. [https://apnews.com/article/mexico-four-men-killed-cancun-police-7247d0942e9a376673ddee0794fc7ec1 (AP)]
*The [[United States Department of Justice]] and the [[Federal Trade Commission]] file a joint [[lawsuit]] against [[TikTok]] and its parent company [[ByteDance]] for violating a law prohibiting companies to collect and use personal information of children under the age of 13. [https://www.reuters.com/technology/doj-faces-friday-deadline-tiktok-children-privacy-suit-2024-08-02/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[End Bad Governance protests]]
**Protests against [[President of Nigeria|President]] [[Bola Tinubu]]'s [[economy of Nigeria|economic]] reforms continue across [[Nigeria]], as [[Nigerian Police|security forces]] fire [[tear gas]] at protestors and the [[Politics of Nigeria|government]] orders curfews across several northern states. '''Sports'''
*[[2024 Summer Olympics]]
**[[Tennis at the 2024 Summer Olympics]]
***[[Novak Djokovic]] defeats [[Lorenzo Musetti]] to advance to the finals of the [[Tennis at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's singles|Men's singles tournament]], becoming the only player to reach the finals four times, and the oldest finalist in [[Tennis at the Olympics|Olympic tennis history]]. [https://www.espn.com/olympics/story/_/id/40709403/novak-djokovic-not-slowed-knee-face-carlos-alcaraz-olympic-men-singles-gold (ESPN)]
***[[Carlos Alcaraz]] defeats [[Félix Auger-Aliassime]] to advance to the finals of the Men's singles tournament, becoming the youngest finalist in Olympic tennis history at 21 years old. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/novak-djokovic-wins-golden-slam-beats-carlos-alcaraz-olympic-mens-singles-title/ (CBS News)]
**[[Individual Neutral Athletes at the 2024 Summer Olympics]]
***[[Belarus|Belarusian gymnast]] [[Ivan Litvinovich]] wins a [[Olympic medal|gold medal]] in [[Gymnastics at the 2024 Summer Olympics#Trampoline|trampoline gymnastics]], making him the first male neutral athlete to win a gold medal at the [[Summer Olympics]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/whale-2024-paris-olympics-surfing-tahiti/ (CBS News)]
